title: Smoke test: chat completion produces a Langfuse trace
description:
Manual flow:
1. Bring up Langfuse compose (already done by task-compose)
2. Bring up uvicorn (02_completed Travel API) and the MCP server
3. Bring up the Angular frontend
4. Log in as Tony Stark, send a single message ("plan me a 3-day Tokyo trip with sushi dinners")
5. Open Langfuse UI -> Traces -> verify a single trace appears within 30 seconds
6. Click into the trace -> verify the tree contains: orchestrator span, at least one sub-agent span, at least one Generation (LLM call), at least one Cosmos retrieval span, and the trace is tagged with user_id=tony, session_id=<the session>

If any of those are missing, file follow-up beads with `--deps discovered-from:<this-bead-id>`.
acceptance_criteria: A trace appears in the Langfuse UI for one chat completion, with the expected span tree and user/session tags. Screenshot or written confirmation captured in this bead.

- redis           (queues + caches)

Pin all images to specific minor tags (NOT :latest) so the workshop is reproducible. Capture chosen tags in a comment block at the top of the file.

Prefer placing the compose stack OUTSIDE the application source trees (i.e. at repo root `langfuse/`) so both 01_exercises and 02_completed can share one local instance. This avoids accidentally documenting two parallel stacks for workshop attendees.

Port mapping: 3000:3000 (web). All other services bind to localhost or are internal-only.

title: ADR: LangSmith evaluate() -> Langfuse Datasets/Evaluations mapping
description:
The three evaluation scripts (01_exercises/evaluation/{e2e,routing,tool_usage}_evaluation.py) currently use `langsmith.Client` to: (1) create or fetch a dataset, (2) upload examples from a JSON file, (3) call `client.evaluate(target_fn, data=dataset, evaluators=[...])` which handles batching, parallelization, and result aggregation, returning a results object.

Langfuse equivalent (decided pattern):
1. `lf = Langfuse()` (auto-reads env vars)
2. Dataset bootstrap: `lf.create_dataset(name=..., description=..., metadata=...)` then for each example `lf.create_dataset_item(dataset_name=..., input=..., expected_output=...)`. Idempotency: catch the "already exists" exception and skip; we do not want re-runs to duplicate items.
3. Run loop: `dataset = lf.get_dataset(name); for item in dataset.items: with item.run(run_name=...) as trace: out = target_fn(item.input); for ev in evaluators: score = ev(item, out); lf.score(trace_id=trace.id, name=ev.name, value=score)`
4. Result aggregation: collect scores in a local dict; print summary table at the end. No built-in equivalent to LangSmith's `experiment_results.to_pandas()`; if needed we will add a `_summarize(scores)` helper.

Parallelization: LangSmith `evaluate` runs concurrent workers. For Langfuse port we will use `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor` with a default of 4 workers, configurable via env var `LANGFUSE_EVAL_CONCURRENCY`. Each worker still creates its own item.run() context manager.

Evaluator function shape: keep current signature `(example, prediction) -> {"key": str, "score": float, "comment": str}`. Adapter writes that into `lf.score(name=..., value=..., comment=...)`.
acceptance_criteria: Pattern is finalized. The bootstrap-helper bead can use this ADR to design the dataset upload helper. The three port tasks can use this ADR to do the rewrite without re-deciding the API.
notes:
DECISION: Pattern locked. One shared helper module
01_exercises/evaluation/_lf_runner.py exposes async run_eval(target,
dataset_name, evaluators, run_name, ...) and upsert_dataset(...). The
three eval scripts each become a thin wrapper around run_eval().

KEY REVISIONS from bead description:

(1) Concurrency: asyncio.Semaphore(N), NOT ThreadPoolExecutor. The
existing target functions are async (await graph.ainvoke), so threads
would force multi-loop chaos. Default N=4, env-overridable via
LANGFUSE_EVAL_CONCURRENCY.

(2) Evaluator signature is (inputs, outputs, reference_outputs) -> SCALAR
(bool/float/int), NOT (example, prediction) -> dict as the bead said.
Sync evaluators use 2-arg form (output, reference_output). Adapter
normalizes bool->0/1 and casts to float.

(3) Tracing during eval is now ON (was hard-disabled today). With
self-hosted Langfuse the perf cost is sub-ms/span and the value of full
agent traces attached to every eval row is the whole point. This is a
behavior change but a strict improvement.

(4) Idempotent upsert REPLACES the e2e script's delete-and-recreate.
Run history is preserved across executions - matches Langfuse Datasets
UI design.

(5) Score name = evaluator function __name__ (matches LangSmith).
Aggregation = local print of mean+count per evaluator; UI is the truth.

DOWNSTREAM CONSUMPTION:
- task-eval-bootstrap (kjf) builds _lf_runner.py per Decision section 1+3
- task-eval-e2e/routing/tool replace aevaluate(...) block with
  await run_eval(...) and Client(...) bootstrap with upsert_dataset(...).
- Evaluator modules under evaluators/ are NOT modified (no LangSmith
  imports; signatures reused as-is).

Full ADR at docs/adr/0003-langsmith-evaluate-to-langfuse-datasets.md
including 5 alternatives considered and the open questions list.

title: ADR: @traceable -> @observe mapping policy
description:
The codebase uses ~95 `@traceable` decorator sites across 6 files. We need ONE consistent mapping rule the rewrite tasks can apply mechanically without per-site judgement.

Decided mapping:
- `@traceable`                          -> `@observe()`
- `@traceable(run_type="llm")`          -> `@observe(as_type="generation")`
- `@traceable(run_type="retriever")`    -> `@observe()` PLUS metadata tag set inside the function via `langfuse.update_current_observation(metadata={"langfuse_legacy_type": "retriever"})` OR a custom label. Langfuse v3 has no first-class retriever span type.

Import change at top of every affected file:
- Remove: `from langsmith import traceable`
- Add:    `from langfuse import observe`

Rationale for full rewrite over shim:
- A shim (`from langfuse import observe as traceable`) would hide the migration from future readers and leave landmines if `traceable` is ever called with LangSmith-only kwargs (e.g., `client=`, `project_name=`).
- The rewrite is mechanical and amenable to find-and-replace; risk is low.
- Workshop attendees benefit pedagogically from seeing native Langfuse APIs in the example code.

Out of scope for this ADR: whether to add new metadata enrichment (user_id, session_id propagation). That is handled in the LangGraph callback story.
acceptance_criteria: Mapping table is finalized and any rewrite task can be executed by following this ADR without further design discussion. If a site cannot be mapped mechanically (e.g., uses `@traceable(name=...)` or `@traceable(metadata=...)`), it is enumerated in this bead as an exception list with the chosen handling.
notes:
DECISION: Pure 1:1 mechanical mapping. No shim, no metadata workaround.

  @traceable                          -> @observe()
  @traceable(run_type="llm")          -> @observe(as_type="generation")
  @traceable(run_type="retriever")    -> @observe(as_type="retriever")

REVISION from bead default: Inspection of langfuse-python v4 source
(langfuse/_client/observe.py) confirms 'as_type=\"retriever\"' is a
first-class supported value (alongside generation/span/agent/tool/chain/
embedding/evaluator/guardrail). The original bead description assumed no
native retriever type and called for a metadata workaround; that
assumption is OBSOLETE on v4 (per ADR-0001). Mapping is now purely
mechanical with NO in-body modifications required.

INVENTORY: 100 sites total across 6 files (was estimated ~95). All sites
use one of three syntactic forms - no name=, metadata=, tags=, client=,
or other kwargs anywhere. Exception list is EMPTY.

REWRITE RECIPE (for task-rw-* tasks): replace parameterized forms BEFORE
bare form so regex ordering doesn't double-rewrite. Also delete the
'logging.getLogger(\"langsmith.client\").setLevel(...)' line in both
mcp_http_server.py files. Collapse the duplicate
'from langsmith import traceable' on lines 11 AND 15 of
01_exercises/python/src/app/services/azure_cosmos_db.py to a single
'from langfuse import observe'.

Out of scope (handled in callback story 7bl.7): user_id/session_id
propagation via propagate_attributes() context manager.

Full ADR at docs/adr/0002-traceable-to-observe-mapping.md including all
4 alternatives considered (shim, metadata workaround, drop retriever,
drop generation) and the per-file rewrite recipe.

title: ADR: Langfuse Python SDK major version pin
description:
We must pin a Langfuse SDK major version in requirements.txt and 01_exercises/pyproject.toml. v3 is the current major (released as a refactor onto OpenTelemetry semantics under the hood); v2 is the prior, more battle-tested major.

Default decision: pin `langfuse>=3.0.0,<4`. v3 keeps the @observe() decorator API identical to v2 from a user-code perspective, supports `as_type="generation"` for LLM spans, and has first-class langchain integration via `langfuse.langchain.CallbackHandler`.

Fallback: if v3 has friction during implementation (e.g., observe(as_type=...) signature change, or LangChain handler import path differences), fall back to `langfuse>=2,<3` and document why in this bead's notes.
acceptance_criteria: A version constraint is committed in all four dependency files (02_completed root requirements.txt, 02_completed/python/src/app/requirements.txt, 01_exercises/requirements.txt, 01_exercises/pyproject.toml) and a one-paragraph justification is appended to this bead before any rewrite tasks start.
notes:
DECISION: pin langfuse>=4.0.0,<5 in all four dependency files
(02_completed/requirements.txt, 02_completed/python/src/app/requirements.txt,
01_exercises/requirements.txt, 01_exercises/pyproject.toml).

Justification: Langfuse v4 was released March 2026 (PyPI latest 4.5.1) and
is the current major. v4 keeps the @observe() decorator API identical to
v3, requires Python >=3.10 (compatible with our 3.11+ floor), and ships
with smart default span filtering plus the observation-centric data model
(propagate_attributes) which is a better fit for our multi-agent graph.
Verified that 'from langfuse.langchain import CallbackHandler' resolves
on v4 (langfuse/langchain/CallbackHandler.py present in repo).

Bead's original default of >=3,<4 was rejected because we are greenfield
and have no v3 code to migrate from, so the v4 breaking changes
(update_current_trace decomposition, namespace remap) cost us nothing
while gaining smart span filtering and the new attribute propagation model.

Full ADR document committed at docs/adr/0001-langfuse-sdk-version.md
including alternatives considered, consequences, and a fallback clause
to v3 if v4 hits blocking friction during implementation.

title: Replace LangSmith with self-hosted Langfuse
description:
Migrate the travel-multi-agent-workshop project end-to-end from LangSmith to a self-hosted Langfuse stack for LLM observability, tracing, and evaluation. Scope covers BOTH the workshop exercise scaffold (01_exercises) AND the completed solution (02_completed). LangSmith dependency must be removed entirely; no shim or compatibility layer is acceptable per scope decision.

Why this matters:
- Self-hosted observability keeps trace data (which can include user PII embedded in conversations and prompts) on infrastructure we control.
- Langfuse is open-source and avoids the LangSmith per-seat pricing model that scales poorly for a shared workshop environment.
- Workshop attendees can run the entire stack offline without external API key dependencies, which has been a recurring pain point (LangSmith 403s observed in the running uvicorn logs even before this migration started).

Scope decisions captured up-front (see decision beads under this epic):
- Hosting: self-hosted Langfuse via local Docker Compose (NOT cloud.langfuse.com, NOT Azure-hosted).
- Decorator strategy: full rewrite of every @traceable to @observe (NO shim like `from langfuse import observe as traceable`).
- Evaluation: port the three evaluation scripts (e2e, routing, tool_usage) to the Langfuse Datasets/Evaluations API.
- Frontend: zero changes (verified no LangSmith refs in frontend/).
- Out of scope: production Azure-hosted Langfuse, historical trace data migration from any existing LangSmith project.
notes:
Branch: `langfuse` (already created by user before scoping started).
Reference plan markdown: ~/.copilot/session-state/67645a35-569f-4d78-8fe5-c41b299bd6a3/plan.md (this bead graph supersedes that document and should be self-contained going forward).
Pre-existing context: project is mid-merge-resolved; main was merged with origin/main (commit 8a795f2 pushed before this branch was cut). Cosmos DB firewall fix already applied. Cosmos key rotation is a known follow-up tracked separately (NOT part of this migration).

title: Build dataset-bootstrap helper module
description:
Create `01_exercises/evaluation/_langfuse_helpers.py` (single underscore prefix to mark internal). Provide:

    def get_or_create_dataset(lf: Langfuse, name: str, description: str = "") -> str
    def upload_examples(lf: Langfuse, dataset_name: str, examples: list[dict], input_key: str, expected_key: str) -> int
    def run_evaluation(lf: Langfuse, dataset_name: str, target_fn, evaluators: list[Callable], run_name: str, max_workers: int = 4) -> dict[str, list[float]]

This consolidates the boilerplate so each of the three port tasks is reduced to: load JSON, define target_fn, define evaluators, call run_evaluation(), print summary.

Idempotency: get_or_create_dataset must NOT raise if the dataset already exists; upload_examples must skip items that match by hash to avoid duplicating on rerun.
design:
Skeleton:

    from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
    from langfuse import Langfuse

    def run_evaluation(lf, dataset_name, target_fn, evaluators, run_name, max_workers=4):
        dataset = lf.get_dataset(dataset_name)
        scores = {ev.__name__: [] for ev in evaluators}
        def _process(item):
            with item.run(run_name=run_name) as trace:
                pred = target_fn(item.input)
                for ev in evaluators:
                    s = ev(item, pred)
                    lf.score(trace_id=trace.id, name=s["key"], value=s["score"], comment=s.get("comment"))
                    scores[ev.__name__].append(s["score"])
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers) as pool:
            list(pool.map(_process, dataset.items))
        return scores
acceptance_criteria: Helper module exists, has docstrings, and is imported successfully by all three eval port tasks. Unit-level smoke: `python -c "from _langfuse_helpers import run_evaluation"` succeeds.

title: Wire CallbackHandler in 02_completed/python/src/app/travel_agents.py
description:
At module init, instantiate one `LangfuseCallbackHandler` (singleton). When invoking the compiled LangGraph (search the file for `.invoke(`, `.ainvoke(`, `.stream(`, `.astream(`), add it to the RunnableConfig:

    from langfuse.langchain import CallbackHandler
    langfuse_handler = CallbackHandler()  # picks up env vars
    ...
    result = graph.invoke(state, config={"callbacks": [langfuse_handler]})

If the existing call sites already accept a `config=` arg, merge into existing callbacks; do not clobber. Propagate `user_id` and `session_id` from the request context via `langfuse_handler.user_id`/`session_id` (set per-invocation) OR by passing metadata in the RunnableConfig - the latter is preferred because it is request-scoped and won't bleed across concurrent requests.
acceptance_criteria: A chat completion produces a trace in the Langfuse UI that contains BOTH the explicit @observe spans from cosmos_db / mcp / travel_agents AND the auto-captured LangGraph internals (chain steps, tool calls, LLM generations).
notes: Verify the CallbackHandler is thread-safe per Langfuse docs; FastAPI uses a thread pool for sync handlers. If not safe, instantiate per-request instead of singleton.

title: Wire LangfuseCallbackHandler into LangGraph configs
description:
The `@observe` decorators only capture the explicit hand-instrumented spans. To get parity with what LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2=true used to give us automatically (every chain/tool/LLM step inside LangGraph), we must register Langfuse's LangChain CallbackHandler and pass it into the LangGraph invocation config.

This is a small but essential plumbing task; without it, traces will look much sparser than they did under LangSmith.
